page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ads_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the EADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, configured with 1 physical core, 2 threads per core, and a total of 2 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 154 GB SSD and supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by strong single-core CPU capabilities but limited multi-core and memory bandwidth performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test ranks in the top 25%, and single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, reflecting the physical single-core constraint. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% and uncached large block read/write speeds in the bottom 25%. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also rank in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4-2ads_v5 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside bundled local SSD storage, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing. The primary tradeoff is the low multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth performance relative to the generous RAM allocation. This server is best suited for memory-bound, single-threaded applications, lightweight caching layers, or small-scale database workloads where memory capacity is prioritized over high-throughput multi-core execution.
